The answer is $50\binom{100}{50}$. The encoding uses binary strings in $\mathbb{F}_2^{100}$. The relation $v \subseteq w$ means $w$ has 1's wherever $v$ does. $f(v)$ counts elements $x \in \bigcup S_i$ with $x \in S_i \iff v_i = 1$.

The divisibility condition becomes $P(u): |u|$ divides $\sum_{v\supseteq u} f(v)$ for $u \neq 0...0$, plus $f(1...1)>0$. We minimize $A := \sum_{|v|\geq 50} f(v)$ over $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$.

The construction is $f_0(v) = 2|v|-100$. For $|u|=100-k$ with $k\leq 50$, the sum equals $(100-k)\cdot 2^k = |u|\cdot 2^k$, a multiple of $|u|$. The objective becomes $50\binom{100}{50}$.

For the smoothing: push-down requires $f(v)\geq |v|$, affects $w\subseteq v$ with $|w|=|v|-1$, increasing $f(w)$ by 1. $P(u)$ affected when $u\subseteq v$: net change $-|u|$. For $|v|>50$, $A$ unchanged (one term down by $-|v|$, $|v|$ terms up by 1).

Apply pushdowns on $1...1$, then $|v|=99$ until $f(v)<99$, then $|v|=98$ until $f(v)<98$, etc., until $f(v)<50$ for $|v|=50$. Then $0\leq f(v)<|v|$ for $|v|=99,...,50$. By downward induction on $50\leq|v|\leq 100$, $f(v)\equiv f_0(v)\pmod{|v|} \implies f(v)=f_0(v)$ since $f_0(v)$ and $f(v)$ are both less than $|v|$. So $f=f_0$.
